messages:
lucas: dropping a prototype for the 'swap & rollback' flow when changing autoscale profiles. goal: reduce accidental cost spikes and make rollback clear. screenshot: https://figma.com/file/abc

mira: nice direction. two quick concerns: the rollback CTA sits under the confirmation and might be missed. can we surface a small inline affordance next to the pool name: 'Preview rollback options'?

dena: also the cost preview card looks dense. users in tests wanted a clear delta number and an absolute monthly estimate. current shows only % change.

infra-bot: FYI: when switching from shared-pool to reserved-high, backend may schedule live migrations. typical migration window 15-45s; retry logic will replay 95% of requests.

a11y: accessibility flag: the modal opens with inert background but focus trap is not implemented in prototype. keyboard users can tab out.

lucas: thanks. proposal: small inline preview under pool selector: 'Cost change: +18% (~$320/mo) · Migration: 15–45s'. clicking the preview expands an explainer panel with rollback options.

mira: prefer showing absolute estimate first: '$320/mo (+18%)' — percentages are secondary. Also add an icon to indicate estimate confidence low/med/high.

dena: UX question: what happens if autoscale is currently increasing capacity while user swaps profile? we should show a combined forecast and a safe suggestion: 'Consider pausing autoscale during swap'.

infra-bot: correct: simultaneous autoscale and profile swaps can cause transient overcommit. runtime will throttle extra requests but may increase billable GPU time. we can detect conflict and surface a guardrail.

lucas: design idea: if conflict detected, show a non-blocking banner: 'Autoscale activity detected. Swap may incur extra cost. Pause autoscale during swap.' with two quick actions: 'Pause autoscale' and 'Continue anyway'.

mira: wording tweak: 'may incur extra cost' is vague. change to 'may temporarily increase cost due to extra allocation'  make shorter: 'may temporarily increase costs.'

a11y: banner must be reachable by keyboard and announced via aria-live assertive if it appears after user action.

dena: rollback UX: when swap fails we should offer a one-click revert that also shows what changed: 'Reverted to profile: reserved-medium (restored in 12s)'. include small log link.

lucas: agree. also add a checksum line: "Changes: min 2→4, max 8→16, burst on" so reversion is transparent.

mira: copy for confirm button: instead of 'Confirm swap' use 'Swap profiles and preview cost' — too long? maybe two-step: primary 'Swap profiles' secondary 'Show cost preview'.

lucas: two-step seems heavy. I'd keep single CTA 'Swap profiles' and the inline preview should update instantly. if user wants details they click 'view forecast'.

infra-bot: integration note: we can fetch cost forecast in <500ms for cached price tables; for uncached combos we might return approximations and mark confidence 'low'. include API field forecast.confidence.

a11y: forecast panel must include plain-language SR text. example: 'Estimated monthly cost increase: three hundred twenty dollars. Expected migration time between fifteen and forty-five seconds. Most requests are retried automatically.'

dena: QA: ensure the rollback action is audited and emits an event in activity feed with a link to request logs.

lucas: action list i'll take: switch preview to absolute $ first, add confidence indicator, implement non-blocking guardrail banner with actionable pause, surface change checksum in rollback dialog, and add aria-live + focus-trap. will push updated frames as 2105001246.

mira: color/accessibility note: confidence badges should use patterned backgrounds, not only color, for colorblind support. use text 'High / Medium / Low' too.

a11y: confirm: modal focus should land on primary CTA. close button should be reachable but not first in tab order.

infra-bot: reminder: attach sample payload for forecast API: {pool_from: 'shared', pool_to: 'reserved-high', min:2, max:16}

lucas: will add payload and copy snippets in the Figma notes. thanks team :rocket:
